transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes on the calendar, we wanted to run through the renewal options and what the capacity expansion to eu-central would look like.
[00:00:15] Leah (Aurora): Yep thanks Alex, quick context — our Q1 roadmap has more fraud detection and conversational flows in the EU, traffic预计 will increase ~3x so we need a plan for both throughput and compliance.
[00:00:35] Darren (Aurora): Also legal wants to confirm data stays in region for PII paths, and that audit logs are exportable.
[00:00:42] Alex: Totally, I put Samira and Jon on to dig into the perf and the account/ops side. Samira, want to kick off with the region sizing?
[00:00:52] Samira (Redwood SE): Sure — based on the projection Leah shared last week, to hit 3x with 95th perc latency under 250ms you'd be looking at either a reserved pool (we call Redwood Dedicated) sized for that steady state, or a committed hosted plan with burst. There are differences in isolation, SLA, and unit economics.
[00:01:20] Marco (Aurora): Quick Q — is the committed hosted plan data isolated? We can't have cross-tenant logs for some routes.
[00:01:27] Jon (Redwood CSM): Good question. Committed hosted keeps customer data logically separated and we provide per-tenant audit logs; for full physical isolation you'd go Dedicated or Private deployment. We can also apply VPC peering and KMS integration for key control.
[00:01:48] Priya (Aurora Legal): When you say "audit logs" what retention and export formats? Our auditors want console access or S3 exports.
[00:01:56] Alex: We can provide S3 export of logs and provide an SSO view for auditors; retention is configurable — standard is 90 days but add-ons extend to 365. We'll put the SOC2 evidence and the audit playbook in the doc pack.
[00:02:12] Darren: And for eu-central specifically, do you have capacity there now or is it via eu-west? Latency to our region matters.
[00:02:20] Samira: We have host capacity in eu-west and eu-central is available as an opt-in region. For eu-central we've been onboarding a few customers and we can prioritize a dedicated pool there with a lead time of ~3 weeks for provisioning, shorter if it's hosted committed units since that's a software routing change.
[00:02:40] Leah: How does burst billing work? We want predictable spend but also headroom.
[00:02:45] Alex: Two models — committed units with capped overage (predictable) or dedicated reserved GPUs with a monthly commit. Committed units are cheaper per token but might have slightly higher variance under peak without burst credits; reserved Dedicated gives predictable throughput and stronger isolation but higher base price. We'll send a side-by-side example.
[00:03:10] Marco: Is there an ops difference for us to manage? We want minimal engineering lift.
[00:03:15] Samira: Hosted committed is almost zero lift — same API, just to route more traffic to region. Dedicated requires a short onboarding (IAM roles, peering, quotas) and we provide an infra runbook. We can make that as plug-and-play as possible.
[00:03:36] [00:03:42] Priya: On the contract side, if we extend 12 vs 24 months are there price breaks? Also what are termination terms?
[00:03:50] Alex: Yes, 24 months gets better unit pricing and a small credit on onboarding fees. Termination terms are standard — 60 days notice for non-renewal; for early termination we can discuss a prorated exit depending on the committed capacity. I'll have legal draft an amendment with the options.
[00:04:12] Darren: Performance question — our worst-case sequences are 2k tokens with KV-heavy context, how does that affect latency?
[00:04:20] Samira: At long context sizes the runtime chooses alternate kernels and caching behavior — our KV cache helps but at those token lengths you'll see higher 95th perc. That's why we recommended a short perf run with your real prompts to validate. We can run quantized variants to reduce cost while preserving latency.
[00:04:40] Leah: Can we do that perf run in eu-central and have Redwood provide the raw logs? We'll want to compare p95 and p99.
[00:04:48] Samira: Yep — we'll spin up a short 5M token run, capture p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and error rates. We'll share the perf spreadsheet link.
[00:05:05] Alex: There's also an option to do a hybrid: reserve baseline in Dedicated for the heavy routes, and put the rest on committed hosted. That gives predictable SLOs for critical endpoints while keeping unit economics tight.
[00:05:20] Marco: Sounds interesting but more complex. Does Redwood handle routing split logic?
[00:05:25] Samira: Yes, smart routing can send requests by route tags and fall back to other model variants if capacity is constrained. You can pin specific model versions to a route.
[00:05:36] Darren: Any mention of encryption at rest and KMS? We need BYOK for eu data.
[00:05:42] Jon: We support KMS integrations and can do customer-managed keys for the private and dedicated offerings; hosted committed can be configured with BYOK as well for sensitive buckets.
[00:05:55] Priya: We'll need those details in writing for the security review.
[00:05:58] Alex: I'll include the security one-pager and KMS integration doc.
[00:06:05] [00:06:18] Leah: Timeline is tight — we want region live by mid-Jan. Is that realistic?
[00:06:25] Samira: For hosted committed, yes — we can route traffic to eu-central in ~2 weeks once we confirm quotas. For a Dedicated pool in eu-central, plan for ~3 weeks to provision and an additional week for validation. So mid-Jan is feasible if we start ASAP.
[00:06:43] Alex: Name the dependencies: decision on 12 vs 24 months, security signoff, and traffic projection.
[00:06:50] Leah: We'll aim to decide on the term by the 18th.
[00:06:55] [00:07:12] Marco: On cost — if we commit 500k tokens/day for 12 months, what's the delta vs 24 months?
[00:07:20] Alex: Rough estimate: 24-month commitment reduces unit price ~8-12% depending on model family and quantization. We'll send precise banding in the pricing doc.
[00:07:32] Darren: Are there any penalties for exceeding committed units in a month?
[00:07:36] Jon: Overage is billed at a predictable rate; we can cap monthly overage and discuss a forgiveness band for the first few months during migration.
[00:07:47] Priya: Procurement will push for a cap and SLA credits.
[00:07:52] Alex: We can agree to an SLA with credits; I'll put the SLA matrix and credit terms in the amendment.
[00:08:02] [00:08:20] Marco: Technical deep dive — what about KV caching and how you'd handle session affinity? We have use-cases that benefit from warm caches.
[00:08:27] Samira: Our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and affinity routing. We can reserve sticky sessions to an instance pool for specific endpoints for a short TTL to keep latency consistent. There are tradeoffs with batching efficiency though.
[00:08:44] Marco: Can we observe cache hit rates?
[00:08:47] Jon: Yes, Console exposes token-level breakdowns, cache hit/miss, per-route metrics; we can add your dashboard to the trial account.
[00:08:58] Leah: About compliance, do you support data residency for derivative artifacts like embeddings?
[00:09:05] Samira: Embeddings follow the same placement rules; if you pin a route to eu-central embeddings and KV live in-region, they won't be replicated outside unless explicitly configured.
[00:09:15] Darren: Ok. Next, migration windows — we expect a 48 hour migration window with rollback capability. What's Redwood's strategy?
[00:09:23] Jon: We'll provide a runbook with canary rollout (1%), quick rollback, and automatic fallback to a previous model variant. We'll also provide a test harness for the QA team to validate pre-cutover.
[00:09:36] [00:09:50] Priya: On the legal docs, any unusual clauses on IP or usage? We need to ensure ownership of derivative models produced by our prompts.
[00:09:58] Alex: Standard usage terms apply; we'll confirm language around derivatives and include a clause that customer retains rights to outputs derived from their data. Legal will draft the exact wording.
[00:10:10] Marco: One last infra question — do you support private deployment options if regulators require it?
[00:10:16] Samira: Yes, Redwood Private is available; that's the fully customer-controlled control plane with on-prem or VPC deployment. That path is more involved and typically for larger accounts.
[00:10:27] Leah: For now we'd prefer hosted committed + Dedicated for critical routes, unless legal pushes Private.
[00:10:33] Alex: Makes sense. We'll prepare both a primary recommendation and contingency for Private.
[00:10:40] [00:10:58] Darren: Can you confirm RPO/RTO expectations in case of region outage?
[00:11:05] Jon: For hosted committed, we provide region-level failover and can route traffic to another region with an expected RTO of a few minutes but with higher latency; we'll document the exact RPO in the runbook. For Dedicated, we can set multi-region redundancy as part of the solution.
[00:11:22] Priya: We'll need that in SLO language for the amendment.
[00:11:27] Alex: Noted.
[00:11:35] [00:11:50] Leah: Ok let's talk timeline again — if we lock 24 months, can you reduce the onboarding lead time for dedicated in eu-central?
[00:11:58] Samira: We can prioritize provisioning for a contract commit and provide a more aggressive timeline, yes. We'll need to align infra slots.
[00:12:08] Marco: Are there any reference customers in finance using eu-central dedicated?
[00:12:12] Alex: We can share a couple of anonymized references — I'll include those in the follow-up email.
[00:12:20] Darren: One more — does Redwood provide per-token cost breakdown by model variant? We want to optimize for cheaper variants for non-critical flows.
[00:12:28] Samira: Console gives token-level cost by route and model; Redwood Optimize will also recommend quantization and model family choices. We'll show a sample optimization report.
[00:12:41] [00:12:55] Priya: Back to pricing, please include onboarding credits and any pilot discounts.
[00:12:59] Alex: We'll include pilot discounts in the first 3 months and a small onboarding credit for 24-month deals.
[00:13:09] Leah: Good. Any risks we should call out?
[00:13:13] Samira: Risk: if models change or a new architecture needs different kernels, perf might shift; we mitigate with pre-commitment perf runs and fallback to compatible variants. Also quota provisioning delays are a scheduling risk.
[00:13:27] Marco: A note — sometimes transcription shows KV cache as "K V cash" in our notes, just a heads up.
[00:13:32] Alex: (laughs) noted.
[00:13:35] [00:13:50] Jon: I'll capture runbook items and put them in the shared folder.
[00:13:54] Darren: On legal — Priya will take point, but we may need to run redlines through procurement.
[00:14:00] Priya: Yep will do.
[00:14:05] [00:14:20] Alex: Alright let's recap next steps quickly: pricing tiers from me, perf run from Samira, runbook from Jon, projected traffic from Leah, legal redlines from Priya. Anything else?
[00:14:34] Leah: No, that covers it.
[00:14:38] Alex: Great — we'll target the week of Nov 16 for the follow-up with preliminary numbers. Thanks everyone.
[00:14:45] Darren: Thanks.
[00:14:48] Marco: Thanks.
[00:14:50] Priya: Bye.
[00:15:00] [END OF TRANSCRIPT SNIPPET]

Notes: Transcript shows periodic timestamps up to ~14m here but call continued for detailed follow-ups and contract discussion; detailed perf logs and pricing were promised as attachments. Some transcription artifacts present (product names slightly garbled).
